standard_prerequisites.name: Perfect graphs and the parameters omega, chi, alpha and theta
standard_prerequisites.statement: A graph is perfect when every induced subgraph H satisfies omega(H)=chi(H), where omega is the size of a largest complete subgraph and chi is the chromatic number; equivalently the complement satisfies alpha(H)=theta(H), where alpha is the size of a largest independent set and theta is the minimum number of cliques covering the vertex set; retained at source lines 100-105.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted corollary is stated for perfect graphs and bounds the two partitions by the ceiling of the logarithm of omega(G) and of alpha(G), so all four parameters and their equality must be available.

standard_prerequisites.name: Theorem A on partitioning an edge set into bipartite graphs
standard_prerequisites.statement: The minimum number of bipartite graphs needed to partition the edge set of a graph G is the ceiling of the base-2 logarithm of chi(G); the article states this as Theorem A at source lines 154-155 and attributes it to Harary, Hsu and Miller.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof applies this theorem twice: once to G itself using chi(G)=omega(G), and once to the graph H left after deleting the edges of a clique cover, using chi(H) <= alpha(G).

standard_prerequisites.name: Weak perfect graph theorem and the clique cover by alpha(G) complete subgraphs
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a perfect graph the complement is perfect, so the vertex set can be partitioned into alpha(G) complete subgraphs, and the union of those complete subgraphs is a single comparability graph; the article invokes this in the proof at source lines 170-172 and describes comparability graphs at source lines 117-120.
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the one comparability graph of part (ii) and the estimate chi(H) <= alpha(G) for the graph H obtained by deleting its edges.

core_obligations: Prove part (i): since chi(G)=omega(G) for a perfect graph G, Theorem A partitions the edge set of G into the ceiling of the base-2 logarithm of omega(G) bipartite graphs (source lines 167-169).

Prove part (ii), first term: by the weak perfect graph theorem the vertex set of G can be partitioned into alpha(G) complete subgraphs, and their union is a single comparability graph (source lines 170-172).

Prove part (ii), remaining terms: delete from G the edges of those complete subgraphs to obtain a graph H, and bound chi(H) <= alpha(G), because the alpha(G) complete subgraphs form a colouring of the complement and hence cover every edge of H by a set of at most alpha(G) complete subgraphs (source lines 172-174).
Apply Theorem A to H: its edge set is partitioned into at most the ceiling of the base-2 logarithm of alpha(G) bipartite graphs, which are in particular comparability graphs (source lines 173-175).
Combine the one comparability graph with the bipartite ones to cover the whole edge set by 1 + the ceiling of the logarithm of alpha(G) comparability graphs, which is part (ii) (source line 175).

proof_roadmap.step: Apply Theorem A to G using chi(G)=omega(G) to get part (i).
Cover the vertex set of G by alpha(G) complete subgraphs and take their union as one comparability graph.
Delete those edges, obtaining H with chi(H) <= alpha(G).
Apply Theorem A to H and add the single comparability graph to conclude part (ii).

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2408.13523v2 的 Corollary genupbound（源 159-164 行，证明 166-175 行，共 10 行）：对任意完美图把边集分别剖成 ⌈log ω(G)⌉ 个二部图与 1+⌈log α(G)⌉ 个可比图。关键操作不是例行核验：(ii) 的第一项要求把弱完美图定理用成「顶点集可剖成 α(G) 个完全子图，其并是同一个可比图」（170-172 行），接着必须论证删去这些完全子图后剩下的图 H 满足 χ(H)<=α(G)——因为那些完全子图正是补图的一个着色，从而按其数量给出 H 的着色数上界（172-174 行），再对 H 用 Theorem A 得到 ⌈log α(G)⌉ 个二部可比图；两处对 Theorem A 的调用分别用的是 χ(G)=ω(G) 与 χ(H)<=α(G)，参数的替换必须各自独立论证。原文位置在证明的 170-174 行。

editorial_notes: The counted unit is the article's own Corollary genupbound at source lines 159-164 together with the author's proof that opens with the bold header Proof. at source line 166 and closes with the square at source line 175; the author separates the two by the sentence at source line 158, which introduces the corollary, so the pairing is by adjacency through the intervening blank line only.

The retained context at source lines 100-105 is the article's own definition of perfect graphs and of the four parameters omega, chi, alpha and theta; the retained context at source lines 117-120 and 128-129 is its own description of comparability graphs and its definitions of p(G) and c(G).

The retained context at source lines 154-155 is the article's own statement of Theorem A on partitioning an edge set into bipartite graphs, which the proof applies twice. The surrounding sentences that carry bibliographic citations are deliberately not retained, so the material carries no bibliography.

The source preamble cannot be retained as it stands: it loads rawfonts, psfrag, verbatim, tikz with several libraries, hyperref with the pagebackref option and a dvi driver option for graphicx, none of which the retained body spans use, and it redefines backref commands that only exist because of that hyperref option. The retained preamble file therefore carries, line for line, source line 2, source line 3, source line 4, source line 16, source line 17, the theorem declarations of source lines 20-30 and the author macro definitions of source lines 32-41; the only textual change anywhere is the removal of the dvipdfm driver option from the graphicx line, because the assembly forces the xelatex engine. No new macro, package or declaration was introduced.

The counted corollary's own itemize environment is standard LaTeX and needs no additional package. The article's other results, including Theorem twocover, Theorem gensplit, Theorem bipline, Theorem unit, Theorem co-triangulated, Theorem loglog, Theorem ub, Lemma rec and Proposition H9, are not counted here.
